gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Sun Gold Power SPH6548P inverter ships with BMS communication off (item 32 defaults to Disable), or that it only reads the SG48100P battery bank after item 32 is set to 485 or CAN and item 33 to the SGP protocol code.
standout_why: ChatGPT's answer says only that separate battery and inverter systems 'require careful electrical design and compatible equipment'. Its 17 results are Tesla Powerwall 3 pages and datasheets plus one EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra page. Those are all-in-one systems, so they never deal with pairing a separate inverter and battery, choosing a protocol, or sizing the DC breaker. None of the 17 were marked cited. I ran out of my tool-call budget before opening the Tesla and EcoFlow pages themselves, so I judged them from their titles and what each product is. I scored this 2, not 3: the settings are new and needed for battery-managed charging, but the inverter can still run the battery without the link using voltage limits the user sets in USER mode, so the protocol alone does not decide whether the set works.
kit_items: inverter: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P 6.5 kW 48 V split-phase (120/240 V) inverter-charger. Its item 33 list includes SGP = SUNGOLDPOWER, so it talks to Sun Gold's own batteries over RS485 or CAN without a third-party protocol.

battery: 2 × Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2 V 100 Ah server-rack LiFePO4 (10.24 kWh). The store says it has CAN/RS485/RS232 and lists SunGoldPower among the compatible inverters. The 48 V nominal class matches the SPH6548P's 48 V input.

DC breaker: Sun Gold Power 160 Amp DC Breaker. This matches the 2P-160A breaker that the SPH6548P manual's cable table lists for the battery side (150 A max current, 35 mm² / 2 AWG cable). Rough check: 6,500 W ÷ 48 V ≈ 135 A.
bus bar: Sun Gold Power 250A Bus Bar with Cover, 48 VDC (1 pair), to join the two SG48100P packs before the single 160 A breaker. 250 A is more than the 150 A inverter battery current.

findings.label: Item 32 BMS communication: options and default
findings.value: Options: enable BMS communication over RS485, enable it over CAN, or Disable (the default). The manual says: 'Select the corresponding communication protocol in item 33 when you set it to 485 or CAN in item 32'
findings.source_title: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P User Manual, page 43 (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: ManualsLib's text extraction scrambles the table layout, so the 485 and CAN labels were not clearly matched to their lines. The 'Disable' default and the item 32 → item 33 instruction are clear. The maker's own copy is https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0323/4090/2025/files/6.5KW_48V_Split_Phase_Solar_Inverter_SPH6548P-20260511.pdf (dated 2026-05-11). I downloaded it but could not extract its text here.
